subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Metal ingot
hotspots.description: A polished metal ingot — a typical metal sample: smooth, solid, and gleaming. This one could be copper or iron.
hotspots.positionHint: The smooth metallic ingot at the center of the scene.
hotspots.function: Shows a real metal sample with its classic look.

hotspots.label: Luster
hotspots.description: The gleam on the ingot is luster — the shiny quality of metals that polished surfaces reflect light strongly.
hotspots.positionHint: The bright highlight on the ingot's upper face.
hotspots.function: Marks the shiny luster that metals are known for.

hotspots.label: Free electrons
hotspots.description: The drifting dots are the metal's free electrons — loose outer electrons that wander between atoms and carry heat and electricity.
hotspots.positionHint: The small drifting dots moving through the ingot, visible when the free-electrons layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the loose electrons that make metals conductive.

hotspots.label: Metal region of the table
hotspots.description: The highlighted zone on the periodic table is where metals live — the left side and the middle, covering about 80% of the elements.
hotspots.positionHint: The large highlighted zone on the table section below the ingot.
hotspots.function: Shows where metals sit on the periodic table.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The metal ingot floats centered above a section of the table, lit with soft neutral studio light — the ingot may carry a gentle soft-specular gleam (that IS its point), but no glow, no bloom, no emissive. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the ingot is a warm metallic copper-grey at moderate roughness (not chrome-saturated), the table tiles are warm paper-white. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / coral / slate / molecular green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=1 ONLY on the ingot (it is the one object in the chemistry set that should read as true metal), roughness ~0.25 so it shows a soft polished gleam without mirror-chrome. Everything else metallic=0: table tiles paper-white roughness ~0.55, free-electron dots muted teal roughness ~0.4. No emissive channels anywhere — any pulse or highlight is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a metal ingot with its loose electrons, built to be read as 'the shiny, conductive workhorse of the elements.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: one smooth rounded rectangular ingot at the center (like a gold-brick shape, ~1.4 x 0.8 x 0.6, corners softly rounded), warm copper-grey metal material with a soft polished gleam. This is the star of the scene.

2) FREE ELECTRONS (toggleable layer): ~10 tiny muted-teal dots (radius ~0.05) drifting slowly through the ingot's volume (the app animates gentle wander paths) — the loose conduction electrons.

3) TABLE REGION (toggleable layer): below the ingot, a flat section of periodic table (grid of paper-white tiles, ~9 columns x 5 rows). The tiles of the left 2 columns and the center block are given a faint muted warm-green cast and slight raise, marking the metal region; a thin stair-step boundary hints where nonmetals would begin.

Camera: framed so the ingot is large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: MetalIngot, FreeElectron_01-10, TableSlab, MetalRegion, StepBoundary. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
